shared_elements: tall upright monolithic stone slab with carved face
row of repeated/paired motifs across the upper register
broader top block over a narrower tapering body
justification: Both are tall, upright carved monoliths whose surfaces are divided into an upper register of repeated paired motifs (bracket/crescent forms in A, symmetrical curvilinear shapes in B) above a lower field containing discs, arcs and a horizontal banded division, and both share the silhouette of a wider top block over a tapering body. The decisive difference is in rendering and content: A's shallow, linear reliefs are legible zoomorphic figures — quadrupeds, long-necked birds, a snake-like form — on a pale, flat-faced slab, whereas B's carving is a rounded, worn, abstract-geometric arrangement of rings and bosses on a dark, three-dimensionally modelled block, so the resemblance stays at the generic level of "decorated standing stone".
